papers.title: Trends in Comorbidities and Fatalities Among First-Time Hepatitis B Hospitalizations in Poland (2012-2023).
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND The clinical profile of patients hospitalized with hepatitis B virus (HBV) is increasingly influenced by coexisting conditions and death patterns. This study aimed to assess comorbidities and fatality rates among patients hospitalized for the first time with HBV between 2012 and 2023. MATERIAL AND METHODS A 12-year retrospective nationwide analysis of first-time HBV hospitalizations in Poland was conducted using data from the Nationwide General Hospital Morbidity Study. RESULTS Digestive diseases (15.6%), cardiovascular diseases (10.5%), and endocrine and metabolic disorders (9.6%) were the most prevalent comorbidities. Between 2012 and 2023, marked increases were observed in digestive (12.3%-27.4%) and metabolic (8.5%-18.5%) disorders, while circulatory diseases rose from 7.4% to 18.6% with post-2019 stabilization. Immune-related and genitourinary disorders demonstrated sustained post-2019 growth, whereas several categories, including neoplasms and respiratory diseases, showed growth-decline patterns. Hypertension and liver fibrosis were the most frequent individual diagnoses, with sustained or stepwise increases over time. Age-stratified analyses revealed a shift from infection-related conditions in younger patients toward cardiometabolic and advanced hepatic diseases in older groups. Fatality rates increased from 6.8-15.9 per 1000 hospitalizations (2012-2019) to 23.1-30.7 per 1000 (2020-2023), peaking during 2020-2021, with higher mortality in men. CONCLUSIONS First-time HBV hospitalizations are increasingly characterized by multimorbidity and rising fatality rates, particularly in older patients. These findings highlight a growing clinical and public health burden, underscoring the need for integrated, age-tailored management and improved surveillance to reduce mortality and optimize HBV care.

papers.title: Serum HBsAg cannot distinguish cccDNA activity from integrated HBV DNA expression in chronic hepatitis B virus infection.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND & AIMS: HBsAg is currently used as the key serum biomarker to define functional cure of chronic hepatitis B (CHB). Declining HBsAg is often interpreted as evidence of cccDNA elimination or durable transcriptional silencing. However, HBsAg can also be produced from transcriptionally active HBV DNA integrated into the host genome (iDNA), which can make serum HBsAg an unreliable indicator of the cccDNA activity or amount. METHODS: We combined intrahepatic HBsAg immunostaining, quantitative serum HBsAg levels (qHBsAg), and digital droplet PCR-based profiling of HBV DNA and RNA in liver biopsies to identify patients in whom HBsAg expression was predominantly driven by cccDNA or by iDNA. We then compared HBsAg abundance, isoform composition, secretion, and intrahepatic staining patterns between these groups. RESULTS: All three envelope proteins (L, M, S) were detectable in liver tissue and serum in both groups. The relative abundance of L and S, assessed by western blot and immunofluorescence, did not differ between iDNA- and cccDNA-driven cases. Across the combined cohort, intrahepatic HBsAg burden correlated with serum qHBsAg, indicating similar intracellular retention and secretion behavior. Importantly, all established intrahepatic HBsAg staining patterns (membranous and cytoplasmic subtypes) occurred in both groups, with no pattern uniquely associated with either source. CONCLUSIONS: Thus, iDNA can sustain HBsAg expression profiles that are indistinguishable from those generated by active cccDNA. Serum HBsAg alone may therefore fail to identify patients who have achieved cccDNA elimination or durable silencing. These findings suggest that the use of serum qHBsAg as a component of the functional cure endpoint in clinical studies warrants re-evaluation. IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: Serum hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) is the central biomarker used to define and monitor "functional cure" in chronic hepatitis B. This study shows that in patients with substantial HBV DNA integration, HBsAg is produced predominantly from integrated sequences, and that integration-derived HBsAg is indistinguishable from cccDNA-derived HBsAg in isoform composition, secretion behaviour, and histological distribution. Long-read sequencing confirmed that the integrated sequences generate full-length envelope transcripts. These findings are most relevant to virologists, hepatologists, clinical trialists, and regulators developing and evaluating HBV cure strategies. They indicate that serum HBsAg measurement cannot report cccDNA burden or transcriptional activity, and that focusing on HBsAg loss could miss "partial cure" states with favourable clinical outcomes. This warrants re-evaluation of HBsAg loss as a main functional cure endpoint, and supports the use of complementary or source-specific markers to assess treatment response.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate whether serum HBsAg can reliably distinguish between cccDNA activity and integrated HBV DNA expression in chronic hepatitis B virus infection, as HBsAg is currently used as a key biomarker for defining functional cure.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted on a combined cohort of patients with chronic hepatitis B virus infection, analyzing intrahepatic HBsAg burden and serum qHBsAg levels to assess their correlation and behavior.
analysis.methods: The researchers used intrahepatic HBsAg immunostaining, quantitative serum HBsAg levels (qHBsAg), and digital droplet PCR to profile HBV DNA and RNA in liver biopsies. They also performed long-read sequencing to confirm the generation of full-length envelope transcripts from integrated sequences.
analysis.main_results: All three envelope proteins (L, M, S) were detectable in both liver tissue and serum in patients with HBsAg expression driven by either cccDNA or integrated HBV DNA. The relative abundance of L and S proteins did not differ between the two groups, and all established HBsAg staining patterns occurred in both groups without unique associations.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that integrated HBV DNA can produce HBsAg profiles indistinguishable from those of active cccDNA, suggesting that serum HBsAg levels alone may not accurately reflect cccDNA status or transcriptional activity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings indicate that serum HBsAg measurement may not be sufficient to assess cccDNA elimination or durable silencing, highlighting the need for complementary or source-specific markers in evaluating treatment response for chronic hepatitis B.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-only evidence, and the design does not include detailed statistical analyses or long-term follow-up. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the reliance on indirect measures and the absence of direct causal conclusions.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景与目的:HBsAg 目前被用作定义 慢性乙型肝炎 或 慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)的关键血清生物标志物。HBsAg 下降通常被解释为 共价闭合环状DNA 消除或持久转录沉默的证据。然而,HBsAg 也可以由整合到 宿主 基因组 (iDNA) 中的转录活性 HBV DNA 产生,这可能使血清 HBsAg 成为 共价闭合环状DNA 活性或数量的不可靠指标。方法:我们结合肝内 HBsAg 免疫染色、定量血清 HBsAg 水平 (qHBsAg) 以及肝活检中基于数字微滴 PCR 的 HBV DNA 和 RNA 分析,以确定 HBsAg 表达主要由 共价闭合环状DNA 或 iDNA 驱动的患者。然后我们比较了这些组之间的 HBsAg 丰度、亚型组成、分泌和肝内染色模式。结果:两组的肝组织和血清中均可检测到所有三种包膜蛋白(L、M、S)。通过蛋白质印迹和免疫荧光评估,L 和 S 的相对丰度在 iDNA 驱动的病例和 共价闭合环状DNA 驱动的病例之间没有差异。在组合的 队列研究 中,肝内 HBsAg 负荷与血清 qHBsAg 相关,表明细胞内滞留和分泌行为相似。重要的是,所有已建立的肝内 HBsAg 染色模式(膜亚型和细胞质亚型)均出现在两组中,没有与任一来源唯一相关的模式。结论:因此,iDNA 可以维持 HBsAg 表达谱,该表达谱与活性 共价闭合环状DNA 产生的表达谱无法区分。因此,仅凭血清 HBsAg 可能无法识别已实现 共价闭合环状DNA 消除或持久沉默的患者。这些发现表明,在临床研究中使用血清 qHBsAg 作为 功能性治愈 终点的组成部分值得重新评估。影响和意义:血清乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg) 是用于定义和监测 慢性乙型肝炎 中“功能性治愈”的核心生物标志物。这项研究表明,在存在大量 HBV DNA 整合的患者中,HBsAg 主要由整合序列产生,并且整合衍生的 HBsAg 与 共价闭合环状DNA 衍生的 HBsAg 在异构体组成、分泌行为和组织学分布方面无法区分。长读长测序证实整合的序列产生全长包膜转录本。这些发现与病毒学家、肝病学家、临床试验人员以及制定和评估乙肝治疗策略的监管机构最为相关。他们表明,血清 HBsAg 测量无法报告 共价闭合环状DNA 负担或转录活性,并且关注 HBsAg 消失可能会错过具有良好临床结果的“部分治愈”状态。这需要重新评估 HBsAg 丢失作为主要 功能性治愈 终点,并支持使用补充或源特异性标记物来评估 治疗 反应。

papers.title: Hepatitis B virus seroprevalence, associated factors, and liver fibrosis burden among people living with HIV in Uganda: a systematic review
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and HIV coinfection remains an important cause of liver-related morbidity and mortality in sub-Saharan Africa. Uganda carries a substantial burden of both infections, yet evidence on HBV seroprevalence, associated factors, and liver fibrosis among people living with HIV (PLHIV) has not been comprehensively synthesized. This systematic review aimed to summarize available evidence from Uganda on HBV seroprevalence, correlates of HBV infection, and liver fibrosis burden among PLHIV. Methods This systematic review was conducted and reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, African Journals Online (AJOL), WHO Global Index Medicus, Google Scholar, and medRxiv/bioRxiv from inception to December 2025 for studies conducted in Uganda among PLHIV reporting HBsAg seroprevalence, factors associated with HBV infection, or liver fibrosis outcomes. Eligible studies included observational designs. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed methodological quality using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal tools. Findings were synthesized narratively. Results A total of 14 studies were included. Most studies were cross-sectional and were conducted in Northern Uganda, Central Uganda, South-Western Uganda, and Lake Victoria fishing communities. Reported HBsAg seroprevalence among PLHIV varied across settings, with higher estimates generally observed in Northern Uganda and fishing communities than in some urban clinic-based populations. Frequently reported factors associated with HBV infection included male sex, older age, lower CD4 cell count, and rural or high-risk residence. Studies assessing liver fibrosis suggested a greater burden of significant fibrosis among HBV-HIV coinfected individuals compared with HIV-monoinfected populations, although fibrosis definitions and diagnostic methods varied substantially across studies. Conclusions Available evidence indicates that HBV infection remains a significant comorbidity among PLHIV in Uganda, with substantial variation in seroprevalence across geographic settings. Male sex, older age, lower CD4 cell count, and residence in higher-burden settings were among the most frequently reported associated factors. Studies also suggest a greater burden of liver fibrosis among HBV-HIV coinfected individuals than among HIV-monoinfected populations. However, interpretation of findings is limited by methodological heterogeneity and the predominance of cross-sectional studies. Systematic review registration PROSPERO CRD420261349477.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection among people living with HIV (PLHIV) in Uganda, focusing on seroprevalence, associated demographic and clinical factors, and liver fibrosis burden. The central question addresses the extent of HBV coinfection, its correlates, and its impact on liver disease in this population.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines and searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, African Journals Online, WHO Global Index Medicus, Google Scholar, and medRxiv/bioRxiv from inception to December 2025. Eligible studies were observational designs conducted in Uganda among PLHIV, reporting HBsAg seroprevalence, associated factors, or liver fibrosis outcomes. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed methodological quality using JBI critical appraisal tools. Fourteen studies were included, with narrative synthesis of findings.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: HBV infection remains a significant comorbidity among PLHIV in Uganda, with seroprevalence varying substantially across geographic settings. Higher HBsAg seroprevalence was generally observed in Northern Uganda and fishing communities compared to some urban clinic-based populations. Frequently reported factors associated with HBV infection included male sex, older age, lower CD4 cell count, and rural or high-risk residence. Studies assessing liver fibrosis suggested a greater burden of significant fibrosis among HBV-HIV coinfected individuals compared with HIV-monoinfected populations, though definitions and diagnostic methods varied.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Interpretation of findings is limited by methodological heterogeneity, including the predominance of cross-sectional studies and variability in fibrosis definitions and diagnostic methods. The evidence base lacks standardized approaches to assess liver fibrosis and associated factors, which constrains comparability and robustness of conclusions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Standardized diagnostic criteria and longitudinal study designs are needed to accurately quantify HBV seroprevalence, identify risk factors, and assess liver fibrosis burden among PLHIV in Uganda. Surveillance programs should prioritize high-risk settings such as Northern Uganda and fishing communities to target interventions effectively.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review synthesizes evidence on hepatitis B virus (HBV) coinfection among people living with HIV (PLHIV) in Uganda, focusing on seroprevalence, associated factors, and liver fibrosis burden. Findings indicate substantial geographic variation in HBV seroprevalence, with higher rates in Northern Uganda and fishing communities. Male sex, older age, lower CD4 cell count, and rural or high-risk residence were frequently reported correlates of HBV infection. Liver fibrosis burden appeared greater in HBV-HIV coinfected individuals than in HIV-monoinfected populations, though diagnostic heterogeneity limited comparability. The review highlights the need for standardized methods and longitudinal studies to improve understanding and guide targeted interventions.

elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: HBV infection remains a significant comorbidity among PLHIV in Uganda, with seroprevalence varying substantially across geographic settings. papers.title_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒 血清流行率、乌干达艾滋病毒感染者的相关因素和肝纤维化负担:系统评价
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and HIV coinfection remains an important cause of liver-related morbidity and mortality in sub-Saharan Africa. Uganda carries a substantial burden of both infections, yet evidence on HBV seroprevalence, associated factors, and liver fibrosis among people living with HIV (PLHIV) has not been comprehensively synthesized. This systematic review aimed to summarize available evidence from Uganda on HBV seroprevalence, correlates of HBV infection, and liver fibrosis burden among PLHIV. Methods This systematic review was conducted and reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, African Journals Online (AJOL), WHO Global Index Medicus, Google Scholar, and medRxiv/bioRxiv from inception to December 2025 for studies conducted in Uganda among PLHIV reporting HBsAg seroprevalence, factors associated with HBV infection, or liver fibrosis outcomes. Eligible studies included observational designs. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed methodological quality using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal tools. Findings were synthesized narratively. Results A total of 14 studies were included. Most studies were cross-sectional and were conducted in Northern Uganda, Central Uganda, South-Western Uganda, and Lake Victoria fishing communities. Reported HBsAg seroprevalence among PLHIV varied across settings, with higher estimates generally observed in Northern Uganda and fishing communities than in some urban clinic-based populations. Frequently reported factors associated with HBV infection included male sex, older age, lower CD4 cell count, and rural or high-risk residence. Studies assessing liver fibrosis suggested a greater burden of significant fibrosis among HBV-HIV coinfected individuals compared with HIV-monoinfected populations, although fibrosis definitions and diagnostic methods varied substantially across studies. Conclusions Available evidence indicates that HBV infection remains a significant comorbidity among PLHIV in Uganda, with substantial variation in seroprevalence across geographic settings. Male sex, older age, lower CD4 cell count, and residence in higher-burden settings were among the most frequently reported associated factors. Studies also suggest a greater burden of liver fibrosis among HBV-HIV coinfected individuals than among HIV-monoinfected populations. However, interpretation of findings is limited by methodological heterogeneity and the predominance of cross-sectional studies. Systematic review registration PROSPERO CRD420261349477.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Evaluation of Hepatitis B Awareness, Knowledge Gaps, Health-Seeking Behaviour, Risk Perceptions, and Vaccination Status Among University Students in Bangladesh: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a significant public health problem globally. In Bangladesh, viral hepatitis is the most common liver disease, with approximately 10 million people infected with HBV. Methods The study was a cross‐sectional survey in which 440 respondents were randomly selected using Cochran's formula. The duration of the study was about 6 month (24th August 2024 to 28th February 2025). Data was gathered using a predesigned and structured questionnaire, which was distributed among the students. The collected data were then analysed utilizing Microsoft Excel 2016 and Stata 17 software for statistical processing and interpretation. Results Overall, the study found that respondents had a high level of awareness of hepatitis B, with most participants recognizing the disease and its major transmission routes and health consequences. Vaccine‐related knowledge was moderate, whereas hepatitis B vaccination uptake remained relatively low among the respondents and their family members. The mean (±SD) awareness, vaccine knowledge, and perception scores were 37.18 ± 11.16, 25.00 ± 10.88, and 22.38 ± 4.71 (each measured on a 50‐point scale), respectively. Multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that male participants were more likely to be vaccinated against hepatitis B than female participants (aOR = 1.74, 95% CI: 1.14–2.67). Participants with low awareness also had higher odds of being vaccinated than those with high awareness (aOR = 2.17, 95% CI: 1.09–4.36), while no significant association was observed for moderate awareness. Conclusion Less than half of the respondents had received the hepatitis B vaccine, with the most common reason for non‐vaccination being a lack of awareness of their vaccination status. Slightly over half of the respondents demonstrated satisfactory knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding hepatitis B. These findings underscore the need for targeted education on hepatitis B infection, its risk factors, and the importance of vaccination among students in Bangladesh.

papers.title: Geospatial Discrepancy of Chronic Hepatitis B and Hepatitis D Testing in Alberta: A Population-Based Spatial Analysis.
papers.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and hepatitis D virus (HDV) coinfection are major causes of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. The geographic distribution of CHB and alignment of anti-HDV testing with CHB burden remain poorly defined. We aimed to examine if anti-HDV testing and seropositivity align with areas of highest CHB burden. Adults with CHB (2014-2022) were identified using a validated serologic algorithm in the provincial laboratory database capturing HBV/HDV serology. Cases were geolocated to Aggregate Dissemination Areas (ADAs), linked to Alberta Health Services zones and rural-urban continuum levels. Age- and sex-standardized CHB prevalence was calculated per ADA using the 2016 Canadian Census. Descriptive mapping, global spatial autocorrelation and local hotspot analysis were used to assess spatial clustering. Among 8317 persons with CHB, the provincial age- and sex-standardized prevalence was 1.70 per 1000 population (95% CI, 1.66-1.74). Prevalence ranged from 2.15 per 1000 in metropolitan areas to 0.40 per 1000 in remote regions and was higher in Calgary than Edmonton (2.53 vs. Overall, 17.5% of CHB patients were tested for anti-HDV, and 4.1% of those tested were anti-HDV positive. CHB prevalence hotspots were concentrated in metropolitan ADAs, whereas hotspots of anti-HDV testing and positivity showed only partial overlap with these high-burden areas. CHB burden in Alberta is geographically clustered, particularly within specific neighbourhoods of metropolitan cities, whereas anti-HDV testing remains infrequent and only partially aligned with high-burden areas. Reflex or systematic anti-HDV testing, paired with geographically informed outreach, may improve case detection.

CHB burden in Alberta is geographically clustered, particularly within specific neighbourhoods of metropolitan cities, whereas anti-HDV testing remains infrequent and only partially aligned with high-burden areas. Reflex or systematic anti-HDV testing, paired with geographically informed outreach, may improve case detection.

papers.title: Single-Cell Hepatitis B Sequencing Reveals Distinct Viral Infection Events Consistent With Superinfection.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The high error rate of the hepatitis B virus (HBV) polymerase leads to a genetically diverse quasispecies in individuals with chronic hepatitis B. Data regarding the propagation of these variants in individual hepatocytes may provide insight into viral replication and diversity of covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA), which is the template for HBV replication. METHODS: We developed sequencing protocols to characterize HBV diversity between and within hepatocytes using RNA extracted from individually isolated hepatocytes. We sequenced HBV in >200 hepatocytes in 4 liver biopsies from people with HIV/HBV (HB1, HB2, HB3, HB6). RESULTS: We found that 2 biopsies (HB1 and HB6) showed HBV diversity between hepatocytes that met an experimentally identified threshold. Specifically, in HB1, HBV sequences from 86 individual cells were from 2 different haplotypes of genotype D: 70.2% of cells with haplotype a, 5.8% with haplotype b, and 24% with both haplotypes in the same cell. Furthermore, within single hepatocytes, up to 3 different HBV sequences were present per cell, including some cells with both genotypes A and D. HB6, who received years of lamivudine monotherapy, had evidence of drug resistance mutations distributed among hepatocytes and demonstrated up to 3 different sequences, including wild-type and drug-resistant sequences, in the same hepatocyte. Modeling of infected hepatocytes did not reveal evidence of local HBV spread based on spatial proximity. CONCLUSIONS: Taken together, our findings demonstrate that individual hepatocytes may harbor multiple, transcriptionally active HBV cccDNA molecules, which likely arose from distinct infection events.

papers.title_zh: 单细胞乙型肝炎测序揭示了与重复感染一致的独特病毒感染事件。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: The high error rate of the hepatitis B virus (HBV) polymerase leads to a genetically diverse quasispecies in individuals with chronic hepatitis B. Data regarding the propagation of these variants in individual hepatocytes may provide insight into viral replication and diversity of covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA), which is the template for HBV replication. METHODS: We developed sequencing protocols to characterize HBV diversity between and within hepatocytes using RNA extracted from individually isolated hepatocytes. We sequenced HBV in >200 hepatocytes in 4 liver biopsies from people with HIV/HBV (HB1, HB2, HB3, HB6). RESULTS: We found that 2 biopsies (HB1 and HB6) showed HBV diversity between hepatocytes that met an experimentally identified threshold. Specifically, in HB1, HBV sequences from 86 individual cells were from 2 different haplotypes of genotype D: 70.2% of cells with haplotype a, 5.8% with haplotype b, and 24% with both haplotypes in the same cell. Furthermore, within single hepatocytes, up to 3 different HBV sequences were present per cell, including some cells with both genotypes A and D. HB6, who received years of lamivudine monotherapy, had evidence of drug resistance mutations distributed among hepatocytes and demonstrated up to 3 different sequences, including wild-type and drug-resistant sequences, in the same hepatocyte. Modeling of infected hepatocytes did not reveal evidence of local HBV spread based on spatial proximity. CONCLUSIONS: Taken together, our findings demonstrate that individual hepatocytes may harbor multiple, transcriptionally active HBV cccDNA molecules, which likely arose from distinct infection events.

papers.title: Virologic Response to Antiviral Therapy in Chronic Hepatitis B Patients With High Viral Load: A Real-World Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Current guidelines for chronic hepatitis B (CHB) have progressively expanded antiviral treatment indications, with age > 30 years increasingly being incorporated as an important criterion. However, real-world evidence regarding treatment outcomes in this expanded population remains limited. This study evaluated the 48-week treatment response and its independent predictors in treatment-naïve CHB patients aged > 30 years with a high baseline viral load. This retrospective study included 808 treatment-naïve CHB patients aged > 30 years with baseline HBV DNA ≥ 2000 IU/mL who received first-line nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) monotherapy. Patients were classified into moderately high (MH; ≥ 2 × 10 3 to 7 IU/mL) and extremely high (EH; ≥ 1 × 10 7 IU/mL) viral load groups. Propensity score matching (PSM) and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) were applied to adjust for baseline imbalance. At week 48, the overall virological response (VR) rate was 90.0% (727/808). Among HBeAg-positive patients at baseline, the HBeAg seroclearance and seroconversion rates were 14.0% (59/422) and 11.8% (50/422), respectively. Compared with the MH group, the EH group had significantly lower rates of VR (81.8% vs. 95.5%, p 7 IU/mL were independently associated with a lower likelihood of VR. These associations remained robust after PSM and IPTW adjustment. First-line NA therapy achieved a favourable 48-week VR in CHB patients aged > 30 years with a high viral load. However, HBeAg positivity and extremely high viral load were associated with suboptimal response, supporting intensified monitoring and individualised management.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 目前的 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 指南已逐步扩大了 抗病毒药物 治疗 的适应症,年龄 > 30 岁越来越多地被纳入一个重要标准。该研究旨在评估年龄 > 30 岁且基线病毒载量较高的 治疗 初治 CHB 患者的 48 周 治疗 反应及其独立预测因子。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性研究纳入了 808 名年龄 > 30 岁且基线 HBV DNA ≥ 2000 IU/mL 且接受一线核苷类似物 (NA) 单药治疗的 808 名 治疗 初治 CHB 患者。患者被分为中高病毒载量组(MH;≥ 2 × 10 3 至 7 IU/mL)和极高病毒载量组(EH;≥ 1 × 10 7 IU/mL)。
elements_zh.methods: 应用倾向得分匹配 (PSM) 和 治疗 加权逆概率 (IPTW) 来调整基线不平衡。该研究评估了第 48 周时的病毒学应答 (VR) 率,并确定了 VR 的独立预测因素。
elements_zh.main_results: 第 48 周时,总体病毒学应答 (VR) 率为 90.0% (727/808)。与 MH 组相比,EH 组的 VR 发生率显着较低(HBeAg 阳性率为 81.8%),并且极高的病毒载量与 VR 可能性较低独立相关。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为 30 岁以上高病毒载量慢性乙型肝炎患者的管理提供了重要见解,强调需要根据病毒载量和 HBeAg 状态制定定制方法。

papers.title: Differential Hepatitis B Surface Antigen Glycan Isomer Kinetics Between Tenofovir Alafenamide and Entecavir: Hepatocellular Carcinoma Risk Stratification in Hepatitis B e Antigen-Positive Patients.
papers.abstract: Nucleos(t)ide analog (NA) therapy suppresses hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA, but residual hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk persists. O-glycosylated hepatitis B surface antigen glycan isomer (HBsAgGi) uniquely reflects virion burden. We evaluated the impact of tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) versus entecavir (ETV) on 48-week HBsAgGi kinetics and its utility in stratifying HCC risk in 90 NA-naïve patients (ETV: 73; TAF: 17). A favourable response was defined as a reduction or maintenance of low HBsAgGi levels. TAF independently predicted a favourable response compared with ETV (penalised odds ratio 3.60, p = 0.030). A significant interaction occurred between HBeAg status and HBsAgGi response in relation to HCC development (p = 0.038). In HBeAg-positive patients, a poor response was associated with increased HCC risk (hazard ratio 7.34, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.96-20.35, p = 0.001); however, the exact magnitude warrants cautious interpretation due to wide CIs. This association was absent in HBeAg-negative cases. Adding HBsAgGi response to the aMAP score improved long-term HCC prediction exclusively in the HBeAg-positive cohort. As the assay targets genotype C-specific O-glycosylation, the findings cannot be generalised to genotypes A, B, or D. In conclusion, on-treatment HBsAgGi response is a specific surrogate marker for stratifying residual HCC risk in HBeAg-positive patients, and TAF is more effective than ETV in inducing these favourable kinetics.

papers.title: Coverage and determinants of hepatitis B virus vaccine uptake among children aged 12-36 months in Ethiopia: an analysis of the 2016 Ethiopian Demographic and Health Survey.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: In Ethiopia, chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) prevalence is high (∼6%) and infant vaccination targets are unmet. We assessed HBV vaccination uptake and associations with parental sociodemographic and obstetric factors among children (aged 12-36 months) in Ethiopia. METHODS: We utilised the 2016 Ethiopian Demographic and Health Survey. We included a weighted sample of 3,855 children (aged 12-36 month) to assess HBV vaccination coverage level (none, incomplete, and complete) and its spatial distribution. Additionally, we identified associated factors of HBV vaccination coverage level using ordinal logistic regression. RESULTS: Overall, 51.2% of children received complete HBV vaccination, with wide regional variation. Older maternal age (adjusted odds ratio (AOR)=1.05, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.02-1.07), better maternal education level (mean AOR=1.66-2.08), higher household wealth quantile (mean AOR=1.51-2.32), distance to a healthcare facility not a big problem (AOR=1.54, 95% CI: 1.25-1.89), and complete maternal continuum care utilisation (AOR=2.59, 95% CI: 1.25-5.30) were positively associated with HBV vaccination coverage, while higher number of children in the household (AOR=0.86, 95% CI: 0.79-0.92) was negatively associated. CONCLUSIONS: HBV vaccination coverage falls below World Health Organization (WHO) targets in Ethiopia and has substantial regional variation. Targeted vaccination campaigns for mothers in lower socioeconomic groups and larger families may improve vaccination coverage.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Ethiopia faces a high burden of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection (~6%) and has not met infant vaccination targets, creating a need to assess coverage and determinants of HBV vaccine uptake among young children.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional analysis was conducted using the 2016 Ethiopian Demographic and Health Survey, including a nationally representative weighted sample of 3,855 children aged 12–36 months to evaluate HBV vaccination coverage levels and their spatial distribution.
analysis_en.methods: HBV vaccination coverage was categorized as none, incomplete, or complete, and associated factors were identified using ordinal logistic regression to model sociodemographic and obstetric determinants.
analysis_en.main_results: Overall, 51.2% of children received complete HBV vaccination, with substantial regional variation in coverage levels observed across Ethiopia.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights that HBV vaccination coverage in Ethiopia remains below WHO targets and demonstrates marked geographic disparities, underscoring the need for targeted interventions.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that prioritizing vaccination campaigns for mothers with lower socioeconomic status and larger families could improve HBV vaccine uptake among children in Ethiopia.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and reliance on survey data may introduce recall or reporting biases, warranting cautious interpretation of the associations identified.

papers.title_zh: 埃塞俄比亚 12-36 个月龄儿童 乙型肝炎病毒 疫苗 的覆盖范围和决定因素:对 2016 年埃塞俄比亚人口和健康调查的分析。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: In Ethiopia, chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) prevalence is high (∼6%) and infant vaccination targets are unmet. We assessed HBV vaccination uptake and associations with parental sociodemographic and obstetric factors among children (aged 12-36 months) in Ethiopia. METHODS: We utilised the 2016 Ethiopian Demographic and Health Survey. We included a weighted sample of 3,855 children (aged 12-36 month) to assess HBV vaccination coverage level (none, incomplete, and complete) and its spatial distribution. Additionally, we identified associated factors of HBV vaccination coverage level using ordinal logistic regression. RESULTS: Overall, 51.2% of children received complete HBV vaccination, with wide regional variation. Older maternal age (adjusted odds ratio (AOR)=1.05, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.02-1.07), better maternal education level (mean AOR=1.66-2.08), higher household wealth quantile (mean AOR=1.51-2.32), distance to a healthcare facility not a big problem (AOR=1.54, 95% CI: 1.25-1.89), and complete maternal continuum care utilisation (AOR=2.59, 95% CI: 1.25-5.30) were positively associated with HBV vaccination coverage, while higher number of children in the household (AOR=0.86, 95% CI: 0.79-0.92) was negatively associated. CONCLUSIONS: HBV vaccination coverage falls below World Health Organization (WHO) targets in Ethiopia and has substantial regional variation. Targeted vaccination campaigns for mothers in lower socioeconomic groups and larger families may improve vaccination coverage.

papers.title: Complex dynamics behavior in a generalized diffusive multiple delays within-host model for HBV infection with capsids and adaptive immune response in a heterogeneous viral environment
papers.abstract: Abstract In this paper, we investigate the dynamics of a new chronic hepatitis B model through environmental-driven infection in heterogeneous and homogenous space. The model includes spatial diffusion, five time delays, and a general incidence function. The well-posedness of solutions, including the existence of global solutions, uniqueness, non-negativity, ultimate boundedness, is established. The reproduction numbers for virus infection, CTL immune response, antibody immune response, CTL immune competition and antibody immune competition, respectively, are calculated. By employing the Lyapunov functionals and linearization methods, the threshold conditions on the global stability of the infection-free equilibrium are obtained; and the threshold conditions on the uniform persistence and the global stability of the equilibria for immune-free, antibody response, CTL response and antibody and CTL responses, respectively, are established. The occurrence of Hopf bifurcation of the spatially homogeneous equilibria is also established. An application is provided, and numerical simulations are carried out to illustrate the analytical results and verify the conjectures. Our findings reveal the rich and complex patterns of HBV infection dynamics in vivo, including regular and irregular periodic oscillations. Irregular oscillations may signify immune disorders and allergies. Also, from numerical simulations, it follows that the majority of hepatitis B infection could escape chronic infection.
papers.journal: Mathematical Medicine and Biology: A Journal of the IMA

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究采用了 HBV 感染的广义扩散多重延迟 -宿主 模型,结合了空间扩散、五次时间延迟和通用 发病率 函数。它专注于异质病毒环境中的乙型肝炎病毒感染。
elements_zh.methods: 解的适定性,包括全局解的存在性、唯一性、非负性和最终有界性,均已成立。该模型使用李亚普诺夫函数和线性化方法来确定全局稳定性和均衡持续性的阈值条件。
elements_zh.main_results: 计算病毒感染的繁殖数、CTL 免疫应答、抗体免疫应答、CTL免疫竞争和抗体免疫竞争。该研究还确定了空间均匀平衡的霍普夫分岔的发生。

papers.title_zh: 异质病毒环境中衣壳和适应性 免疫应答 HBV 感染的 宿主 模型内广义扩散多重延迟中的复杂动力学行为
papers.source_body_en: Abstract In this paper, we investigate the dynamics of a new chronic hepatitis B model through environmental-driven infection in heterogeneous and homogenous space. The model includes spatial diffusion, five time delays, and a general incidence function. The well-posedness of solutions, including the existence of global solutions, uniqueness, non-negativity, ultimate boundedness, is established. The reproduction numbers for virus infection, CTL immune response, antibody immune response, CTL immune competition and antibody immune competition, respectively, are calculated. By employing the Lyapunov functionals and linearization methods, the threshold conditions on the global stability of the infection-free equilibrium are obtained; and the threshold conditions on the uniform persistence and the global stability of the equilibria for immune-free, antibody response, CTL response and antibody and CTL responses, respectively, are established. The occurrence of Hopf bifurcation of the spatially homogeneous equilibria is also established. An application is provided, and numerical simulations are carried out to illustrate the analytical results and verify the conjectures. Our findings reveal the rich and complex patterns of HBV infection dynamics in vivo, including regular and irregular periodic oscillations. Irregular oscillations may signify immune disorders and allergies. Also, from numerical simulations, it follows that the majority of hepatitis B infection could escape chronic infection.

papers.title: A New Nomogram for Mortality Prediction Within 5 Years in Portal Vein Thrombosis due to Hepatitis B-Related Cirrhosis.
papers.abstract: This study aims to develop a nomogram model intended for predicting long-term mortality in patients suffering from hepatitis B-related cirrhosis associated with Portal vein thrombosis (PVT). A total of 961 patients were recruited from January 2015 to December 2023, forming the training cohort. We analysed independent risk factors affecting 5-year mortality through COX regression, from which we constructed a nomogram. To assess the nomogram's utility, we employed the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, C-index, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The independent prognostic factors retained in the final model for patients with hepatitis B-related cirrhosis complicated by PVT included age (HR = 1.09, 95% CI: 1.06-1.11; p < 0.001), leukocyte count (WBC) (HR = 1.09, 95% CI: 1.03-1.17; p = 0.002), and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) (HR = 1.29, 95% CI: 1.22-1.35; p < 0.001), along with serum sodium (HR = 0.94, 95% CI: 0.90-0.98; p = 0.005). The AUROC values for the nomogram were 0.906 (95% CI: 0.891-0.921) in the training cohort and 0.910 (95% CI: 0.885-0.927) in the validation cohort, demonstrating improved performance and discriminatory ability compared to current models, including CTP and MELD scores. Age, leukocyte count (WBC), NLR, and serum sodium emerged as independent risk factors impacting prognosis for patients with hepatitis B cirrhosis and PVT within 5 years. The nomogram developed in this research holds significant potential for accurately predicting the outcomes of these patients within 5 years.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the unmet need for accurate long-term mortality prediction in patients with hepatitis B-related cirrhosis complicated by portal vein thrombosis (PVT), a high-risk subgroup with limited prognostic tools.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort of 961 patients with hepatitis B-related cirrhosis and PVT was recruited from January 2015 to December 2023 and formed the training cohort for model development.
analysis.methods: Independent risk factors for 5-year mortality were identified using Cox regression, and a nomogram was constructed from these factors; model performance was assessed with ROC curves, C-index, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis.
analysis.main_results: The nomogram achieved AUROC values of 0.906 (95% CI: 0.891–0.921) in the training cohort and 0.910 (95% CI: 0.885–0.927) in the validation cohort, outperforming Child–Turcotte–Pugh and MELD scores.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the nomogram as a significant advance in individualized risk stratification for this patient group, highlighting its improved discrimination compared to existing scoring systems.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The nomogram could inform clinical decision-making by enabling earlier identification of high-risk patients for intensified monitoring or therapeutic interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The single-centre, retrospective design and lack of external validation limit generalisability; the evidence strength is assessed as moderate due to potential selection and confounding biases.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed a nomogram to predict 5-year mortality in patients with hepatitis B-related cirrhosis complicated by portal vein thrombosis (PVT) using a training cohort of 961 patients. Independent prognostic factors included age, leukocyte count, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and serum sodium. The model demonstrated high discriminatory performance with AUROC values of 0.906 in training and 0.910 in validation, outperforming Child–Turcotte–Pugh and MELD scores. The authors propose the nomogram as a clinically useful tool for individualized risk stratification in this high-risk subgroup.

papers.title: Mixed Cryoglobulinaemic Glomerulonephritis Section Type II in the Setting of Rheumatoid Arthritis and Chronic Hepatitis B: A Case Report
papers.abstract: Mixed (Type II) cryoglobulinaemia is a systemic immune-complex vasculitis often linked to chronic infections especially Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) or autoimmune disease. Chronic Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) associated cryoglobulinaemic is rare, and its coexistence with Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) is especially unusual. The authors report a 45-year-old female with long-standing seropositive RA on methotrexate and chronic HBV presented with fatigue, arthralgias, palpable purpura on her legs, and new-onset oedema. Laboratory workup showed elevated serum creatinine, nephrotic-range proteinuria, hypoalbuminaemia, haematuria, and a positive Rheumatoid Factor (RF). Antinuclear Antibody (ANA) and Anti-double-stranded deoxyribonucleic acid (anti-dsDNA) were negative. Complement levels i.e., Component 3 (C3) moderately reduced, Component 4 (C4) severely low, and positive mixed cryoglobulins with a high Immunoglobulin M (IgM) cryocrit. HCV and Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) serologies were negative. Renal biopsy showed a diffuse endocapillary proliferative, Membranoproliferative Glomerulonephritis (MPGN) with hyaline “pseudothrombi.” Immunofluorescence disclosed granular capillary wall deposits of IgM, Immunoglobulin G (IgG) (both kappa and lambda), C3, and C1q, consistent with Type II cryoglobulinaemic GN. Treatment included high-dose corticosteroids and HBV antiviral drugs. Despite antiviral therapy and plasmapheresis, renal failure progressed requiring haemodialysis, and the patient died within three weeks due to disease-related complications and nosocomial infection. The present case highlights that RA and HBV can together underlie cryoglobulinaemic GN. Early recognition using RF, complement, and cryocrit testing and biopsy-guided therapy are critical. Purpura, positive RF, and low C4/C3 should prompt consideration of mixed cryoglobulinaemic vasculitis.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Mixed cryoglobulinaemic glomerulonephritis (GN) is a systemic immune-complex vasculitis often associated with chronic infections like Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) or autoimmune diseases, but its occurrence in the context of Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) and Chronic Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) is rare and unusual.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This case report describes a 45-year-old female with seropositive RA on methotrexate and chronic HBV who presented with fatigue, arthralgias, palpable purpura, and new-onset oedema. The study focuses on the clinical presentation and diagnostic findings of this unique case.
analysis.methods: The patient underwent laboratory workup, including serological testing for HCV and HIV, and a renal biopsy to assess the histopathological features of the glomerulonephritis. Immunofluorescence was used to identify immune complex deposits.
analysis.main_results: Laboratory tests revealed elevated serum creatinine, nephrotic-range proteinuria, hypoalbuminaemia, haematuria, and a positive Rheumatoid Factor (RF). Complement levels were moderately reduced (Component 3) and severely low (Component 4), with positive mixed cryoglobulins and a high Immunoglobulin M (IgM) cryocrit. Renal biopsy showed diffuse endocapillary proliferative, membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis (MPGN) with hyaline pseudothrombi, and immunofluorescence confirmed granular capillary wall deposits of IgM, IgG (both kappa and lambda), C3, and C1q.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The case highlights that RA and HBV can coexist and contribute to the development of mixed cryoglobulinaemic GN, which is a rare and unusual association. The findings suggest the importance of considering this condition in patients with overlapping autoimmune and viral diseases.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The case underscores the need for early recognition of mixed cryoglobulinaemic vasculitis in patients with RA and HBV, emphasizing the role of RF, complement, and cryocrit testing, as well as biopsy-guided therapy, in managing such complex clinical scenarios.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 45-year-old female with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis (RA) on methotrexate and chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection who developed mixed cryoglobulinaemic glomerulonephritis (GN). Laboratory findings included elevated serum creatinine, nephrotic-range proteinuria, hypoalbuminaemia, haematuria, and a positive rheumatoid factor (RF), with complement levels showing moderate reduction (C3) and severe reduction (C4). However, the study's limitations include its single-case design, which restricts generalizability and causal inference.

papers.title_zh: 类风湿关节炎与慢性乙型肝炎相关的II型冷球蛋白血症性肾小球肾炎分型:一例病例报告
papers.source_body_en: Mixed (Type II) cryoglobulinaemia is a systemic immune-complex vasculitis often linked to chronic infections especially Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) or autoimmune disease. Chronic Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) associated cryoglobulinaemic is rare, and its coexistence with Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) is especially unusual. The authors report a 45-year-old female with long-standing seropositive RA on methotrexate and chronic HBV presented with fatigue, arthralgias, palpable purpura on her legs, and new-onset oedema. Laboratory workup showed elevated serum creatinine, nephrotic-range proteinuria, hypoalbuminaemia, haematuria, and a positive Rheumatoid Factor (RF). Antinuclear Antibody (ANA) and Anti-double-stranded deoxyribonucleic acid (anti-dsDNA) were negative. Complement levels i.e., Component 3 (C3) moderately reduced, Component 4 (C4) severely low, and positive mixed cryoglobulins with a high Immunoglobulin M (IgM) cryocrit. HCV and Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) serologies were negative. Renal biopsy showed a diffuse endocapillary proliferative, Membranoproliferative Glomerulonephritis (MPGN) with hyaline “pseudothrombi.” Immunofluorescence disclosed granular capillary wall deposits of IgM, Immunoglobulin G (IgG) (both kappa and lambda), C3, and C1q, consistent with Type II cryoglobulinaemic GN. Treatment included high-dose corticosteroids and HBV antiviral drugs. Despite antiviral therapy and plasmapheresis, renal failure progressed requiring haemodialysis, and the patient died within three weeks due to disease-related complications and nosocomial infection. The present case highlights that RA and HBV can together underlie cryoglobulinaemic GN. Early recognition using RF, complement, and cryocrit testing and biopsy-guided therapy are critical. Purpura, positive RF, and low C4/C3 should prompt consideration of mixed cryoglobulinaemic vasculitis.
papers.abstract_zh: 混合型(II 型)冷球蛋白血症是一种全身性免疫复合物血管炎,通常与慢性感染尤其是丙型肝炎病毒 (HCV) 或自身免疫性疾病有关。慢性乙型肝炎 病毒 (HBV) 相关的冷球蛋白血症很少见,其与类风湿关节炎 (RA) 共存尤其罕见。作者报告了一名 45 岁女性,患有长期服用甲氨蝶呤且患有慢性乙型肝炎的血清阳性 RA,并出现疲劳、关节痛、腿部明显紫癜和新发水肿。实验室检查显示血清肌酐升高、肾病范围蛋白尿、低蛋白血症、血尿和类风湿因子 (RF) 阳性。抗核抗体(ANA)和抗双链脱氧核糖核酸(抗 dsDNA)均为阴性。补体水平,即成分 3 (C3) 中度降低,成分 4 (C4) 严重降低,以及具有高免疫球蛋白 M (IgM) 冷比容的阳性混合冷球蛋白。HCV 和人类免疫缺陷病毒 (HIV) 血清学结果呈阴性。肾活检显示弥漫性毛细血管内增生性膜增生性肾小球肾炎(MPGN),伴有透明“假血栓”。免疫荧光显示 IgM、免疫球蛋白 G (IgG)(κ 和 lambda)、C3 和 C1q 的颗粒状毛细血管壁沉积,与 II 型冷球蛋白血症 GN 一致。治疗 包括大剂量皮质类固醇和 HBV 抗病毒药物 药物。尽管进行了 抗病毒药物 治疗和血浆置换,肾功能衰竭仍进展需要血液透析,并且患者在三周内因疾病相关并发症和医院感染而死亡。本病例强调 RA 和 HBV 共同构成冷球蛋白血症性肾小球肾炎。使用射频、补体和冷冻比容测试以及活检引导治疗进行早期识别至关重要。紫癜、RF 阳性和 C4/C3 低应提示考虑混合性冷球蛋白血症性血管炎。

papers.title: Validation of a Point-Of-Care Ultrasound for Hepatitis Among Front-Line Healthcare Workers Managing Chronic Hepatitis B Virus Infection in Zambia.
papers.abstract: To close gaps in implementing care of people with hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in resource-limited settings, we evaluated the accuracy of a novel liver point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) protocol for hepatitis (PUSH) among front-line non-radiology healthcare workers in Zambia. At University Teaching Hospital in Lusaka, Zambia, from March to June 2024, we trained four nurses and six physicians with experience in HBV management, but not in ultrasound (US), in the PUSH protocol, which includes visualizing the liver in three windows (epigastric, subcostal and right transcostal) to identify cirrhosis-suggestive features and liver lesions suspicious for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Then, consecutive adult participants with chronic hepatitis B (PWHB) alone or HBV/HIV coinfection underwent PUSH with operators blinded to clinical data. We evaluated the accuracy of PUSH for significant fibrosis and cirrhosis using transient elastography (TE) as the reference standard test (RST) and for liver lesions that were possible HCC using a comprehensive abdominal ultrasound by an experienced radiographer as the RST. Nonparametric analysis of the receiver operating curve (ROC) for PUSH was adjusted for operator type (doctor vs. nurse), sex and HIV status. Among 197 PWHBs analysed, 69.5% were taking HBV antivirals and 27.9% had HBV/HIV. According to RSTs, 17.7% of PWHBs had significant fibrosis, 11.6% had cirrhosis and 3.5% had liver lesions. PUSH had low accuracy for significant fibrosis, with sensitivity of 8.3% (17.5-41.4), specificity of 100.0% (96.1-100) and an area under the curve (AUROC) of 0.54 (0.43-0.65), moderate accuracy for cirrhosis, with sensitivity of 60.9% (38.5-80.3), specificity of 97.7% (94.2-99.4) and AUROC of 0.79 (0.69-0.89), and higher accuracy for liver lesions, with 85.7% (42.1-99.6) sensitivity, 98.4% (95.5-99.7) specificity, AUROC of 0.92 (0.78-1.00). After an expedited training, front-line nurses and physicians treating HBV in Zambia were able to use PUSH to diagnose cirrhosis with moderate accuracy and liver lesions with high accuracy, although confidence intervals around performance estimates were wide. Liver POCUS including PUSH may be useful in HBV management when laboratory systems and TE are lacking.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the need to improve hepatitis B virus (HBV) care in resource-limited settings by evaluating a novel point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) protocol (PUSH) for diagnosing HBV-related liver disease among front-line healthcare workers in Zambia.
analysis.study_design_and_population: At University Teaching Hospital in Lusaka, Zambia, from March to June 2024, four nurses and six physicians with HBV management experience but no ultrasound training were trained in the PUSH protocol, which assesses liver cirrhosis-suggestive features and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) lesions in three windows.
analysis.methods: Consecutive adult participants with chronic hepatitis B (PWHB) alone or HBV/HIV coinfection underwent PUSH with operators blinded to clinical data, and accuracy was evaluated using transient elastography (TE) as the reference standard for fibrosis and cirrhosis and comprehensive abdominal ultrasound by an experienced radiographer for liver lesions.
analysis.main_results: Among 197 PWHBs, 17.7% had significant fibrosis, 11.6% had cirrhosis, and 3.5% had liver lesions; PUSH showed low accuracy for significant fibrosis (sensitivity 8.3%, specificity 100.0%, AUROC 0.54), moderate accuracy for cirrhosis (sensitivity 60.9%, specificity 97.7%, AUROC 0.79), and high accuracy for liver lesions (sensitivity 85.7%, specificity 98.4%, AUROC 0.92).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that PUSH can diagnose cirrhosis with moderate accuracy and liver lesions with high accuracy after expedited training, highlighting its potential utility in HBV management where laboratory systems and TE are lacking.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that PUSH could support HBV care in resource-limited settings by enabling front-line healthcare workers to identify cirrhosis and HCC lesions, potentially improving early diagnosis and referral pathways.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s limitations include wide confidence intervals around performance estimates and reliance on a single-center, short-duration training, which may limit generalisability and precision of accuracy metrics.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated a point-of-care ultrasound protocol (PUSH) for diagnosing hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related liver disease among front-line healthcare workers in Zambia. After brief training, nurses and physicians used PUSH to assess liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) lesions in adults with chronic HBV or HBV/HIV coinfection. Using transient elastography and expert ultrasound as reference standards, PUSH showed low accuracy for significant fibrosis (AUROC 0.54), moderate accuracy for cirrhosis (AUROC 0.79), and high accuracy for liver lesions (AUROC 0.92). The authors conclude that PUSH may be useful for HBV management in settings lacking laboratory infrastructure, though confidence intervals were wide and the single-center design limits generalisability.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究通过评估用于诊断赞比亚一线医护人员中 HBV 相关肝病的新型护理点超声 (POCUS) 方案 (PUSH),解决了在资源有限的环境中改善 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 护理的需要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2024 年 3 月至 6 月,在赞比亚卢萨卡的大学教学医院,四名护士和六名具有乙肝管理经验但没有接受过超声培训的医生接受了 PUSH 方案培训,该方案在三个窗口中评估肝硬化提示特征和肝细胞癌 (HCC) 病变。
elements_zh.methods: 单独感染 慢性乙型肝炎 (PWHB) 或 HBV/HIV 合并感染的连续成人参与者在不了解临床数据的操作员的情况下接受 PUSH,并使用瞬时弹性成像 (TE) 作为纤维化和肝硬化的参考标准以及由经验丰富的肝脏病变放射技师进行综合腹部超声评估准确性。
elements_zh.main_results: 197名感染者中,17.7%有明显纤维化,11.6%有肝硬化,3.5%有肝脏病变;PUSH 对显着纤维化的准确性较低(敏感性 8.3%,特异性 100.0%,AUROC 0.54),对肝硬化的准确性中等(敏感性 60.9%,特异性 97.7%,AUROC 0.79),对肝脏病变的准确性较高(敏感性 85.7%,特异性 98.4%,AUROC 0.92)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,经过快速培训后,PUSH 可以以中等准确度诊断肝硬化,并以较高准确度诊断肝脏病变,这突显了其在缺乏实验室系统和 TE 的 HBV 管理中的潜在用途。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,PUSH 可以通过使一线医护人员识别肝硬化和 HCC 病变来支持资源有限环境中的 HBV 护理,从而有可能改善早期 诊断 和转诊途径。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性包括表现估计的置信区间较宽,以及对单中心、短期训练的依赖,这可能会限制准确性指标的普遍性和精度。

papers.abstract_zh: 为弥合资源有限环境中乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染患者护理实施中的差距,我们评估了一种新型肝脏床旁超声(POCUS)肝炎筛查方案(PUSH)在赞比亚一线非放射科医护人员中的准确性。在2024年3月至6月期间,于赞比亚卢萨卡大学教学医院,我们培训了4名护士和6名有HBV管理经验但无超声(US)经验的医生,采用PUSH方案,包括在三个窗口(上腹部、肋下和右侧肋间)观察肝脏,以识别提示肝硬化的特征及疑似肝细胞癌(HCC)的肝脏病变。随后,连续纳入仅患有乙型肝炎(PWHB)或HBV/HIV合并感染的成年参与者,进行PUSH检查,操作者对临床数据不知情。我们使用瞬时弹性成像(TE)作为参考标准(RST)评估PUSH对显著纤维化和肝硬化的准确性,并使用经验丰富放射技师进行的全面腹部超声作为可能HCC肝脏病变的RST。采用非参数法分析PUSH的受试者工作特征曲线(ROC),并按操作者类型(医生vs护士)、性别和HIV状态进行调整。在197名分析的PWHB中,69.5%正在接受HBV抗病毒药物治疗,27.9%为HBV/HIV合并感染。根据RST结果,17.7%的PWHB存在显著纤维化,11.6%存在肝硬化,3.5%存在肝脏病变。PUSH对显著纤维化的准确性较低,敏感性为8.3%(17.5-41.4),特异性为100.0%(96.1-100),曲线下面积(AUROC)为0.54(0.43-0.65);对肝硬化的准确性为中等,敏感性为60.9%(38.5-80.3),特异性为97.7%(94.2-99.4),AUROC为0.79(0.69-0.89);对肝脏病变的准确性较高,敏感性为85.7%(42.1-99.6),特异性为98.4%(95.5-99.7),AUROC为0.92(0.78-1.00)。在赞比亚,经过快速培训的前线护士和医生能够使用PUSH以中等准确性诊断肝硬化,以高准确性诊断肝脏病变,尽管性能估计的置信区间较宽。在缺乏实验室系统和TE的情况下,包含PUSH的肝脏POCUS可能有助于HBV管理。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究通过评估用于诊断赞比亚一线医护人员中 HBV 相关肝病的新型护理点超声 (POCUS) 方案 (PUSH),解决了在资源有限的环境中改善 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 护理的需要。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 2024 年 3 月至 6 月,在赞比亚卢萨卡的大学教学医院,四名护士和六名具有乙肝管理经验但没有接受过超声培训的医生接受了 PUSH 方案培训,该方案在三个窗口中评估肝硬化提示特征和肝细胞癌 (HCC) 病变。
analysis_zh.methods: 单独感染 慢性乙型肝炎 (PWHB) 或 HBV/HIV 合并感染的连续成人参与者在不了解临床数据的操作员的情况下接受 PUSH,并使用瞬时弹性成像 (TE) 作为纤维化和肝硬化的参考标准以及由经验丰富的肝脏病变放射技师进行综合腹部超声评估准确性。
analysis_zh.main_results: 197名感染者中,17.7%有明显纤维化,11.6%有肝硬化,3.5%有肝脏病变;PUSH 对显着纤维化的准确性较低(敏感性 8.3%,特异性 100.0%,AUROC 0.54),对肝硬化的准确性中等(敏感性 60.9%,特异性 97.7%,AUROC 0.79),对肝脏病变的准确性较高(敏感性 85.7%,特异性 98.4%,AUROC 0.92)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,经过快速培训后,PUSH 可以以中等准确度诊断肝硬化,并以较高准确度诊断肝脏病变,这突显了其在缺乏实验室系统和 TE 的 HBV 管理中的潜在用途。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,PUSH 可以通过使一线医护人员识别肝硬化和 HCC 病变来支持资源有限环境中的 HBV 护理,从而有可能改善早期 诊断 和转诊途径。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性包括表现估计的置信区间较宽,以及对单中心、短期训练的依赖,这可能会限制准确性指标的普遍性和精度。

papers.title: Assessing the Status of and Impediments to Achieving the WHO Goal to Eliminate Viral Hepatitis B by 2030: A Scoping Review
papers.abstract: This project registers a scoping review examining progress toward the World Health Organization (WHO) goal of eliminating viral hepatitis B (HBV) as a public health threat by 2030. In 2016, the WHO set targets of a 90% reduction in new chronic infections and a 65% reduction in mortality relative to a 2015 baseline; yet, despite effective vaccines and potent antivirals, viral hepatitis mortality continues to rise. The review assesses the global and regional status of, and impediments to, the 2030 HBV elimination goal, and compares HBV with hepatitis C virus (HCV) elimination trajectories. It was conducted following the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and reported in accordance with the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Peer-reviewed literature, global and regional surveillance reports, and grey literature published between 2015 and 2025 were searched across five databases and multiple institutional repositories, using the JBI Population–Concept–Context (PCC) framework. Charted data were mapped against WHO impact indicators (incidence, mortality, prevalence) and service-coverage indicators (HepB3 and timely birth-dose vaccination, diagnosis, treatment) across the six WHO regions. The specific objectives are: (i) to determine the global and regional status against the WHO 2030 HBV elimination targets; (ii) to evaluate the effectiveness, implementation, and gaps of HBV vaccination strategies (HepB3 and birth dose) and their impact on HBV epidemiology; and (iii) to compare HBV and HCV elimination efforts to identify divergent challenges and transferable opportunities.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the status of and impediments to achieving the WHO goal of eliminating viral hepatitis B (HBV) as a public health threat by 2030. It examines progress toward this goal, evaluates the effectiveness of HBV vaccination strategies, and compares HBV elimination efforts with those for hepatitis C virus (HCV).
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The scoping review was conducted following the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and reported in accordance with the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). It searched peer-reviewed literature, global and regional surveillance reports, and grey literature published between 2015 and 2025 across five databases and multiple institutional repositories, using the JBI Population–Concept–Context (PCC) framework.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Despite the availability of effective vaccines and potent antivirals, viral hepatitis mortality continues to rise. The review maps data against WHO impact indicators (incidence, mortality, prevalence) and service-coverage indicators (HepB3 and timely birth-dose vaccination, diagnosis, treatment) across the six WHO regions to assess progress toward the 2030 elimination targets.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights gaps in HBV vaccination strategies and their implementation, as well as challenges in achieving the WHO targets. It also notes the need for more detailed analysis of HBV elimination efforts compared to HCV, particularly in identifying divergent challenges and transferable opportunities.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review identifies specific priorities for research, surveillance, diagnosis, treatment, and policy to address the ongoing challenges in achieving the WHO goal of eliminating HBV by 2030. These include improving vaccination coverage, enhancing diagnostic and treatment access, and strengthening surveillance systems.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该审查重点关注实现世卫组织到 2030 年消除作为公共卫生威胁的乙型病毒性肝炎 (HBV) 目标的现状和障碍。审查审查了实现这一目标的进展情况,评估了 HBV 疫苗接种 策略的有效性,并将乙型肝炎病毒消除工作与丙型肝炎病毒 (HCV) 消除工作进行了比较。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 范围界定审查是按照 Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) 的方法进行的,并根据 PRISMA 范围界定审查扩展 (PRISMA-ScR) 进行报告。它使用 JBI 人口-概念-背景 (PCC) 框架,在五个数据库和多个机构存储库中检索了同行评审文献、全球和区域 监测 报告以及 2015 年至 2025 年间发表的灰色文献。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 尽管有有效的 疫苗 和强效 抗病毒药物,病毒性肝炎 死亡率 的数量仍在继续上升。该审查根据世卫组织影响指标(发病率、死亡率、患病率)和服务覆盖指标(HepB3 和及时出生剂量 疫苗接种、诊断、治疗)绘制了世卫组织六个区域的数据,以评估实现 2030 年消除目标的进展情况。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查强调了 HBV 疫苗接种 战略及其实施方面的差距,以及实现世卫组织目标的挑战。它还指出,与丙肝病毒相比,需要对乙肝病毒的消除工作进行更详细的分析,特别是在确定不同的挑战和可转移的机会方面。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查确定了研究的具体优先事项、监测、诊断、治疗 和政策,以应对实现世卫组织到 2030 年消除乙型肝炎的目标所面临的持续挑战。其中包括提高 疫苗接种 覆盖率、增强诊断和 治疗 的可及性以及加强 监测 系统。

analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查强调了 HBV 疫苗接种 战略及其实施方面的差距,以及实现世卫组织目标的挑战。它还指出,与丙肝病毒相比,需要对乙肝病毒的消除工作进行更详细的分析,特别是在确定不同的挑战和可转移的机会方面。

papers.title: Liver cirrhosis in Bangladesh: a systematic review of etiology, complications and management gaps
papers.abstract: Liver cirrhosis represents a significant and growing cause of morbidity and mortality in Bangladesh, reflecting the increasing burden of chronic liver diseases in low- and middle-income countries. This systematic review aims to evaluate the current etiological patterns of cirrhosis in Bangladesh, summarize its major complications and clinical outcomes, and identify critical gaps in prevention and management. A comprehensive literature search was conducted across MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and BanglaJOL from database inception to August 29, 2025. Eligible studies included observational studies, clinical trials, and national reports involving Bangladeshi populations with chronic liver disease or cirrhosis. Study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Due to substantial methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively. Of 1,847 identified records, 62 studies met eligibility criteria. Most were single-center hospital-based cross-sectional studies from tertiary centers in Dhaka. Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains the predominant etiology, accounting for 30-60% of cirrhosis cases, while hepatitis C virus (HCV) contributes 5-20%. Recent meta-analyses indicate a pooled HBV prevalence of 4.0% (95% CI: 3.0-5.1%) in the general population. Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD/MASLD) has emerged as a rapidly increasing cause, with community prevalence of 25-35% among adults, rising to over 50% in individuals with metabolic risk factors. Major health system challenges include inadequate HBV/HCV screening, limited access to endoscopy and liver transplantation, insufficient hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) surveillance, and absence of structured NAFLD/MASLD management pathways. Bangladesh is experiencing an epidemiological transition from viral to metabolic causes of cirrhosis, necessitating strengthened viral hepatitis control, expanded metabolic disease prevention, improved specialist services, and establishment of standardized national surveillance programs.

The study highlights the predominance of hepatitis B virus (HBV) as the main cause, contributing 30-60% of cirrhosis cases, with hepatitis C virus (HCV) accounting for 5-20%. The review identifies critical challenges in the healthcare system, including inadequate screening for HBV and HCV, limited access to specialist services, and insufficient surveillance for hepatocellular carcinoma. However, the study's limitations include methodological heterogeneity, which led to narrative synthesis of results. The evidence suggests a transition from viral to metabolic causes of cirrhosis, underscoring the importance of targeted interventions and standardized surveillance programs.

papers.title_zh: 孟加拉国肝硬化:病因学、并发症和管理差距的系统评价
papers.source_body_en: Liver cirrhosis represents a significant and growing cause of morbidity and mortality in Bangladesh, reflecting the increasing burden of chronic liver diseases in low- and middle-income countries. This systematic review aims to evaluate the current etiological patterns of cirrhosis in Bangladesh, summarize its major complications and clinical outcomes, and identify critical gaps in prevention and management. A comprehensive literature search was conducted across MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and BanglaJOL from database inception to August 29, 2025. Eligible studies included observational studies, clinical trials, and national reports involving Bangladeshi populations with chronic liver disease or cirrhosis. Study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Due to substantial methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively. Of 1,847 identified records, 62 studies met eligibility criteria. Most were single-center hospital-based cross-sectional studies from tertiary centers in Dhaka. Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains the predominant etiology, accounting for 30-60% of cirrhosis cases, while hepatitis C virus (HCV) contributes 5-20%. Recent meta-analyses indicate a pooled HBV prevalence of 4.0% (95% CI: 3.0-5.1%) in the general population. Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD/MASLD) has emerged as a rapidly increasing cause, with community prevalence of 25-35% among adults, rising to over 50% in individuals with metabolic risk factors. Major health system challenges include inadequate HBV/HCV screening, limited access to endoscopy and liver transplantation, insufficient hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) surveillance, and absence of structured NAFLD/MASLD management pathways. Bangladesh is experiencing an epidemiological transition from viral to metabolic causes of cirrhosis, necessitating strengthened viral hepatitis control, expanded metabolic disease prevention, improved specialist services, and establishment of standardized national surveillance programs.

papers.title: Functional FOXA2 3’UTR variant rs1055080 is associated with HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma risk and postoperative prognosis
papers.abstract: Hepatocarcinogenesis is predominantly driven by chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. Although the transcription factor FOXA2 is known to regulate hepatic development and metabolism, the impact of its genetic predisposition on HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HBV-HCC) remains unclear. We performed a case-control analysis in 4,921 Chinese participants. Two candidate functional single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) (rs1209523 at the promoter region and rs1055080 at the 3’UTR region) in FOXA2 were genotyped. The functions of FOXA2 SNPs were evaluated by dual-luciferase reporter assays. The prognostic values of FOXA2 SNPs were evaluated in a postoperative cohort study of 367 patients with HBV-HCC. The frequency of the rs1055080-T allele was significantly associated with reduced risk of HBV-HCC. This association was evident when HBV-HCC patients were compared with asymptomatic HBV carriers and patients with chronic hepatitis B. In reporter assays, rs1055080-T showed higher FOXA2 3’UTR reporter activity than rs1055080-C. Reporter constructs carrying the rs1055080-C allele showed stronger repression by miR-328-3p or miR-3615 than those carrying rs1055080-T. rs1055080-T was significantly associated with lower frequencies of HCC-risk HBV mutations. Reporter activity of the rs1055080-C construct decreased in the presence of A1762T/G1764A. rs1055080-CT + TT was associated with better overall survival in HBV-HCC. These findings suggest that the FOXA2 3’UTR variant is a candidate germline marker for risk stratification and prognostic assessment in HBV-infected subjects.

papers.title: Characterising Hepatitis D Virus in the UK From 2011 to 2021.
papers.abstract: Little is known about hepatitis B virus (HBV) and Hepatitis D virus (HDV) coinfection in the UK. HDV screening is recommended among all individuals with HBV, with coinfection associated with increased disease progression. Using data on HDV testing, shared by 11 laboratories in the UK who reported undertaking HDV testing, and national testing data for HBV we established a cohort of individuals tested for HDV, investigating testing pathways, describing characteristics and outcomes of those HDV-RNA positive to inform targeted interventions for testing, diagnosis and linkage to care. Demographic information, clinical assessments, treatment and recent laboratory results from NHS trusts, and through linkage to national healthcare datasets was collected for HDV-RNA positive individuals. Between 2011 and 2021, 42% of individuals newly diagnosed with HBV in England were linked to an HDV test. Anti-HDV positivity was 5.0%, 55.8% were HDV-RNA tested and 45.7% were ever HDV-RNA positive. HDV-RNA positivity in the absence of an anti-HDV result was 6.4%. Among individuals who were HDV-RNA positive, 94.3% were non-UK born, with 24 different primary languages reported, 49% had evidence of treatment, and 48% had evidence of cirrhosis. 10% had died of which 58.4% died of liver disease. In conclusion, our findings indicate that HDV testing in HBV positive individuals in the UK is sub-optimal against testing guidelines, including RNA testing among those who are anti-HDV positive. Considerable work is needed to improve the patient care pathway, to ensure patients are appropriately diagnosed, linked and retained in care, with adequate access to treatment.

papers.title_zh: 2011 年至 2021 年英国丁型肝炎病毒的特征。
papers.source_body_en: Little is known about hepatitis B virus (HBV) and Hepatitis D virus (HDV) coinfection in the UK. HDV screening is recommended among all individuals with HBV, with coinfection associated with increased disease progression. Using data on HDV testing, shared by 11 laboratories in the UK who reported undertaking HDV testing, and national testing data for HBV we established a cohort of individuals tested for HDV, investigating testing pathways, describing characteristics and outcomes of those HDV-RNA positive to inform targeted interventions for testing, diagnosis and linkage to care. Demographic information, clinical assessments, treatment and recent laboratory results from NHS trusts, and through linkage to national healthcare datasets was collected for HDV-RNA positive individuals. Between 2011 and 2021, 42% of individuals newly diagnosed with HBV in England were linked to an HDV test. Anti-HDV positivity was 5.0%, 55.8% were HDV-RNA tested and 45.7% were ever HDV-RNA positive. HDV-RNA positivity in the absence of an anti-HDV result was 6.4%. Among individuals who were HDV-RNA positive, 94.3% were non-UK born, with 24 different primary languages reported, 49% had evidence of treatment, and 48% had evidence of cirrhosis. 10% had died of which 58.4% died of liver disease. In conclusion, our findings indicate that HDV testing in HBV positive individuals in the UK is sub-optimal against testing guidelines, including RNA testing among those who are anti-HDV positive. Considerable work is needed to improve the patient care pathway, to ensure patients are appropriately diagnosed, linked and retained in care, with adequate access to treatment.

papers.title: Hepatitis B surface antigen directly alters Dendritic cell-mediated Natural Killer cell responses.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND & AIMS: Hepatitis B, caused by the Hepatitis B virus (HBV), is a significant global health concern, often leading to chronic hepatitis B in individuals unable to mount an effective immune response. Chronic HBV substantially increases the risk of severe liver diseases, including cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Dendritic cells (DC) and Natural killer (NK) cells play crucial roles in the early immune response to HBV, but their function is compromised in chronic hepatitis B patients. We investigated how Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) influences the interplay between DC subpopulations and NK cells. METHODS: Blood-derived DC subsets were pre-exposed to HBsAg and then co-cultured with NK cells under various stimulation conditions. We subsequently evaluated the modulations of DC, and the phenotypic and functional responses of NK cells. Similarly, DC subsets were exposed to serum from HBV-infected individuals with varying levels of HBsAg or directly purified from HBV patients to assess their ability to stimulate NK cell responses. RESULTS: Our findings show that HBsAg disrupts cDC2-mediated NK cell activation through Toll-like receptor (TLR)7/8-dependent pathways and cDC1-mediated NK cell degranulation via TLR3-dependent mechanisms. Exposure of pDC to HBsAg alters NK cell activation, phenotype and degranulation through TLR9-dependent pathways. This impairment was recapitulated following exposure to serum from HBV-infected patients in an HBsAg-dependent manner. Consistently, circulating HBsAg in patients with chronic HBV infection was associated with impaired pDC-mediated NK cell cytotoxicity. CONCLUSIONS: These results uncover key mechanisms by which HBsAg modulates pDC-NK cell interactions, shedding light on how HBV evades innate immune responses and contributes to immune dysfunction.
papers.journal: Cellular and molecular gastroenterology and hepatology

Dendritic cells (DC) and Natural killer (NK) cells play crucial roles in the early immune response to HBV, but their function is compromised in chronic hepatitis B patients.
analysis.methods: Blood-derived DC subsets were pre-exposed to HBsAg and then co-cultured with NK cells under various stimulation conditions. We subsequently evaluated the modulations of DC, and the phenotypic and functional responses of NK cells. Similarly, DC subsets were exposed to serum from HBV-infected individuals with varying levels of HBsAg or directly purified from HBV patients to assess their ability to stimulate NK cell responses.
analysis.main_results: Our findings show that HBsAg disrupts cDC2-mediated NK cell activation through Toll-like receptor (TLR)7/8-dependent pathways and cDC1-mediated NK cell degranulation via TLR3-dependent mechanisms. Exposure of pDC to HBsAg alters NK cell activation, phenotype and degranulation through TLR9-dependent pathways. This impairment was recapitulated following exposure to serum from HBV-infected patients in an HBsAg-dependent manner. Consistently, circulating HBsAg in patients with chronic HBV infection was associated with impaired pDC-mediated NK cell cytotoxicity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These results uncover key mechanisms by which HBsAg modulates pDC-NK cell interactions, shedding light on how HBV evades innate immune responses and contributes to immune dysfunction.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide insights into the mechanisms of HBV immune evasion and immune dysfunction, which could inform future research on immune modulation and the development of therapeutic strategies for chronic HBV infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on in vitro experiments and does not account for in vivo complexities, which may limit the generalizability of the findings. The evidence is strong as it directly links HBsAg to specific immune cell interactions and impairments.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) influences the interaction between dendritic cells (DC) and Natural Killer (NK) cells in the context of HBV infection. The research highlights that HBsAg disrupts DC-mediated NK cell activation and degranulation through distinct Toll-like receptor pathways. These findings reveal key mechanisms by which HBV evades innate immune responses, contributing to immune dysfunction in chronic infections. The study's results have implications for understanding immune evasion strategies and could guide future research on immune modulation. However, the study is limited to in vitro experiments, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. The evidence is strong and directly supports the conclusions drawn about HBsAg's role in immune impairment.

papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND & AIMS: Hepatitis B, caused by the Hepatitis B virus (HBV), is a significant global health concern, often leading to chronic hepatitis B in individuals unable to mount an effective immune response. Chronic HBV substantially increases the risk of severe liver diseases, including cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Dendritic cells (DC) and Natural killer (NK) cells play crucial roles in the early immune response to HBV, but their function is compromised in chronic hepatitis B patients. We investigated how Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) influences the interplay between DC subpopulations and NK cells. METHODS: Blood-derived DC subsets were pre-exposed to HBsAg and then co-cultured with NK cells under various stimulation conditions. We subsequently evaluated the modulations of DC, and the phenotypic and functional responses of NK cells. Similarly, DC subsets were exposed to serum from HBV-infected individuals with varying levels of HBsAg or directly purified from HBV patients to assess their ability to stimulate NK cell responses. RESULTS: Our findings show that HBsAg disrupts cDC2-mediated NK cell activation through Toll-like receptor (TLR)7/8-dependent pathways and cDC1-mediated NK cell degranulation via TLR3-dependent mechanisms. Exposure of pDC to HBsAg alters NK cell activation, phenotype and degranulation through TLR9-dependent pathways. This impairment was recapitulated following exposure to serum from HBV-infected patients in an HBsAg-dependent manner. Consistently, circulating HBsAg in patients with chronic HBV infection was associated with impaired pDC-mediated NK cell cytotoxicity. CONCLUSIONS: These results uncover key mechanisms by which HBsAg modulates pDC-NK cell interactions, shedding light on how HBV evades innate immune responses and contributes to immune dysfunction.
